stories.headline: EU Delays AI Act High-Risk Rules to December 2027, Bans Nudifier Apps in Omnibus Deal

key_facts.fact: EU Parliament and Council reached a provisional deal early May 7 to postpone high-risk AI system obligations from August 2, 2026 to December 2, 2027 for standalone systems, and August 2, 2028 for AI embedded in products.
key_facts.excerpt: obligations on high-risk AI systems will apply: From 2 December 2027 for AI systems with a high-risk use case... From 2 August 2028 for AI systems used as safety components and covered by EU sectoral legislation

key_facts.fact: The deal largely exempts AI used in industrial applications from the AI Act's scope — a win for Germany after Chancellor Friedrich Merz pushed for the change to keep Siemens and Bosch competitive.
key_facts.excerpt: The Machinery Regulation gets a full exemption from direct AI Act applicability. Instead, the Commission gains power to adopt delegated acts adding health and safety requirements for high-risk AI systems under machinery law.

key_facts.fact: A new prohibition bans AI systems that generate child sexual abuse material or produce non-consensual intimate images of identifiable people (nudifier apps). Companies have until December 2, 2026 to comply.
key_facts.excerpt: Parliament and Council also agreed to ban AI systems that create child sexual abuse material or depict the intimate parts of an identifiable person... without that person's consent.

key_facts.fact: The grace period for AI-generated content watermarking obligations was shortened from six months to three, with a new deadline of December 2, 2026.
key_facts.excerpt: Watermarking obligations on AI-generated content, on the other hand, will apply earlier than the Commission proposed, from Dec. 2, 2026 instead of Feb. 2, 2027

key_facts.fact: It took three rounds of negotiations to reach the deal; a previous session on April 28 collapsed after 12 hours of haggling over how AI in regulated products should be assessed.
key_facts.excerpt: It took three rounds to get there. the failed 28 April session collapsed after roughly twelve hours of haggling over how AI built into regulated products should be assessed for conformity.

key_facts.fact: The deal still requires formal adoption by Parliament and Council before becoming law; co-legislators intend to adopt it before August 2, 2026.
key_facts.excerpt: The provisional agreement needs to be formally adopted by both Parliament and Council before it can enter into law. The co-legislators intend to adopt it before 2 August 2026

stories.headline: Cloudflare Cuts 1,100 Jobs (~20% of Workforce) in Shift to 'Agentic AI-First' Operating Model

key_facts.fact: Cloudflare announced on May 7 it would reduce its workforce by more than 1,100 employees globally, approximately 20% of its 5,156-person workforce.
key_facts.excerpt: We are writing to let you know directly that we've made the decision to reduce Cloudflare's workforce by more than 1,100 employees globally.

key_facts.fact: Cloudflare's internal AI usage increased by more than 600% in the last three months, with employees running thousands of AI agent sessions daily across engineering, HR, finance, and marketing.
key_facts.excerpt: Cloudflare's usage of AI has increased by more than 600% in the last three months alone. Employees across the company from engineering to HR to finance to marketing run thousands of AI agent sessions each day

key_facts.fact: The company expects $140–$150 million in restructuring charges, consisting of $105–$110M in cash severance and $35–$40M in non-cash equity vesting, mostly hitting Q2 2026.
key_facts.excerpt: It had 5,156 full-time employees at the end of 2025, and expects charges between $140 million and $150 million associated with the job cuts in the second quarter.

key_facts.fact: Despite the layoffs, Cloudflare reported Q1 2026 revenue of $639.8M, up 34% YoY, beating estimates of $621.9M. Shares dropped roughly 19% in after-hours trading.
key_facts.excerpt: In the first quarter, Cloudflare reported revenue of $639.8 million, beating analysts' estimate of $621.9 million... Shares of the San Francisco-based company dropped roughly 19 per cent in extended trading

key_facts.fact: Co-founders Matthew Prince and Michelle Zatlyn framed the cuts as a one-time structural reorganization for the 'agentic AI era,' not a cost-cutting exercise or assessment of individual performance.
key_facts.excerpt: Today's actions are not a cost-cutting exercise or an assessment of individuals' performance; they are about Cloudflare defining how a world-class, high-growth company operates and creates value in the agentic AI era.

key_facts.fact: Departing employees receive full base pay through end of 2026, US healthcare through year-end, and equity vesting through August 15 with waived one-year cliffs.
key_facts.excerpt: We are pairing the directness of these measures with severance packages that lead the industry.

stories.headline: AI Translation Startup DeepL Cuts ~25% of Workforce (~250 Staff) Citing AI Restructuring

key_facts.fact: DeepL announced plans to cut approximately 250 employees, about 25% of its 1,000+ person workforce, in a LinkedIn post by CEO Jarek Kutylowski on May 7.
key_facts.excerpt: 'We are reducing DeepL's workforce by about 250 positions,' writes DeepL founder and CEO Jarek Kutylowski on LinkedIn today. The layoffs affect about a quarter of the employees of the Cologne unicorn.

key_facts.fact: Kutylowski attributed the cuts to a 'massive structural shift in what work exists, who does it, and how many people it takes to do it well,' calling it the most difficult decision of his career.
key_facts.excerpt: 'It is the most difficult decision I have had to make in my career,' says the DeepL boss. 'However, it is a conscious structural decision about how DeepL must operate to remain a global leader in AI.'

key_facts.fact: DeepL plans to switch to smaller, self-responsible teams where AI handles routine tasks and employees focus on what 'only humans can bring' — intuition, creative ideas, and end-to-end project ownership.
key_facts.excerpt: 'We are moving to smaller high-agency teams where AI handles the routine, so people can focus on what only humans can bring, like using our intuition, coming up with new creative ideas and seeing projects through from start to finish.'

key_facts.fact: Founded in 2017 as a rival to Google Translate, DeepL was valued at $2 billion in its last funding round in May 2024 and had been considered a US IPO candidate at up to $5B.
key_facts.excerpt: Investors valued the company at two billion US dollars in the last major financing round in May 2024. The Cologne-based start-up was also considered a candidate for a possible IPO in the USA.

stories.headline: ShinyHunters Breaches Canvas Again, Claims 275M Records from 9,000 Schools; Platform Taken Offline

key_facts.fact: Hacking group ShinyHunters defaced Canvas login portals at approximately 330 educational institutions on May 7, displaying an extortion message and setting a May 12 deadline to leak data.
key_facts.excerpt: BleepingComputer has learned that threat actors defaced the Canvas login portals for approximately 330 educational institutions, replacing the standard login pages with an extortion message.

key_facts.fact: ShinyHunters claims to have stolen 275–280 million student and staff records tied to nearly 9,000 schools, universities, and education platforms using Instructure's Canvas LMS.
key_facts.excerpt: After announcing on May 1 that it had exfiltrated several terabytes of data containing the personal information of 275 million users, it announced a deadline of Thursday before 'everything is leaked'

key_facts.fact: Affected institutions include Harvard, MIT, Cambridge, Columbia, Cornell, Georgetown, UC Berkeley, and thousands of K-12 school districts globally including in Australia and the UK.
key_facts.excerpt: The attached list of affected institutions includes many school districts, along with well-known universities, including Cambridge, Columbia, Cornell, Georgetown, Harvard, MIT and UC Berkeley.

key_facts.fact: Compromised data includes names, email addresses, student ID numbers, and user messages; Instructure says no evidence passwords, dates of birth, or financial information were involved.
key_facts.excerpt: Instructure said earlier this week that the leaked information includes names, email addresses, student ID numbers and user messages, but that it has so far 'found no evidence that passwords, dates of birth, government identifiers, or financial information were involved.'

key_facts.fact: Instructure placed Canvas, Canvas Beta, and Canvas Test in maintenance mode after the defacement; the platform had been declared 'fully operational' just one day earlier.
key_facts.excerpt: Instructure posted Wednesday that 'Canvas is fully operational, and we are not seeing any ongoing unauthorized activity.' But by Thursday afternoon, Instructure acknowledged there was trouble again

key_facts.fact: ShinyHunters criticized Instructure for ignoring ransom demands, saying 'our demand was not even as high as you might think it is' and that the company 'seemingly does not care about all the students affected.'
key_facts.excerpt: 'Instructure has not even bothered speaking to us to understand the situation or to negotiate with us to prevent the release of this data. Our demand was not even as high as you might think it is'

stories.headline: Italy's Angelini Pharma Acquires Catalyst Pharmaceuticals for $4.1B to Enter US Rare Disease Market

key_facts.fact: Angelini Pharma agreed to acquire Catalyst Pharmaceuticals for $4.1 billion in cash, paying $31.50 per share — a 21% premium to Catalyst's April 22 closing price.
key_facts.excerpt: Angelini Pharma will acquire Catalyst Pharmaceuticals in a $4.1 billion deal... Angelini will pay $31.50 per outstanding share of Catalyst, a 21% premium to the latter's closing price the day prior.

key_facts.fact: Catalyst markets three approved CNS drugs: Firdapse (Lambert-Eaton myasthenic syndrome, the first FDA-approved treatment), Fycompa (seizures), and Agamree (Duchenne muscular dystrophy), generating $588.8M in 2025 revenue.
key_facts.excerpt: Catalyst, which was established in 2002, has three marketed medicines. Firdapse, approved in 2018, is a pill for patients with Lambert-Eaton myasthenic syndrome... Catalyst brought in $589 million in revenue last year from those drugs, a 20% increase

key_facts.fact: The acquisition marks Angelini Pharma's entry into the US market and is framed as part of a five-year transformation focusing on neurological rare diseases.
key_facts.excerpt: 'Entering the U.S. market will allow us to acquire the scale and capabilities needed to continue this journey'... The acquisition of the biopharmaceutical company... marks Angelini Pharma's entry into the U.S. market.

key_facts.fact: Angelini Industries Group, which owns Angelini Pharma, is a family-controlled Italian company founded in 1919 — making this a pivotal moment in its over-100-year history.
key_facts.excerpt: A statement said the acquisition was a 'pivotal moment' in the Angelini Group's over-100-year-long history, which is chaired by Thea Paola Angelini, a fourth-generation member of the Angelini family.

key_facts.fact: Closing is expected in Q3 2026; Catalyst will operate as an Angelini Pharma subsidiary.
key_facts.excerpt: The companies expect to complete the transaction in the third quarter of this year. When the deal closes, Catalyst will operate as an Angelini Pharma subsidiary.

stories.headline: Nvidia Partners with IREN on 5 GW AI Infrastructure Pipeline; Secures $2.1B Investment Right

key_facts.fact: Nvidia signed a strategic partnership with data center operator IREN to deploy up to 5 GW of DSX-aligned AI infrastructure across IREN's global pipeline.
key_facts.excerpt: Nvidia has signed a strategic partnership with AI cloud and data center operator IREN to deploy up to 5 GW of DSX-aligned AI infrastructure across the company's global pipeline.

key_facts.fact: Nvidia secured a five-year right to purchase up to 30 million shares of IREN stock at $70 per share, creating a potential $2.1 billion investment pathway.
key_facts.excerpt: Nvidia secured a five-year right to purchase up to 30 million shares of IREN stock at $70 per share, creating a potential $2.1 billion investment pathway subject to future conditions and regulatory approvals.

key_facts.fact: IREN's 2 GW Sweetwater campus in Texas is positioned as the flagship deployment for Nvidia's DSX AI factory architecture.
key_facts.excerpt: The deal positions IREN's 2 GW Sweetwater campus in Texas as a flagship deployment for Nvidia's DSX AI factory architecture

key_facts.fact: In a separate release, IREN said it signed a five-year deal worth $3.4 billion to provide Nvidia with managed GPU cloud services for its internal AI and research workloads at its Childress, Texas, data centers.
key_facts.excerpt: IREN said it signed a five-year deal worth $3.4 billion to provide Nvidia with access to managed GPU cloud services 'for its internal AI and research workloads.' The deployment will be at IREN's existing data centers in Childress, Texas.

key_facts.fact: IREN previously signed a $9.7 billion deal with Microsoft in November 2025 and recently acquired cloud software company Mirantis for $625 million.
key_facts.excerpt: The Nvidia partnership follows IREN's $625 million acquisition of Mirantis... adding Kubernetes and cloud operations capabilities to help convert deployed GPUs into enterprise-ready AI services.

key_facts.fact: IREN shares initially surged ~27% on the news before retreating to settle up about 6% in extended trading. The Australian-founded company has transitioned from bitcoin mining to AI infrastructure.
key_facts.excerpt: IREN shares climbed to around 27% as the news broke, then retreated and settled up about 6%... Although IREN previously specialized in data centers that were tailored for bitcoin mining, it's been increasingly providing AI-related infrastructure services

stories.headline: Iran Still Reviewing US Peace Proposal; Trump Threatens Bombing, Saudi/Kuwait Lift Base Restrictions

key_facts.fact: Iran's Foreign Ministry spokesman Esmaeil Baqaei said on May 7 that the US proposal is 'still under review' and Iran will share its position with mediator Pakistan after finalizing its views.
key_facts.excerpt: Iran says US proposal to end the war is still 'under review'... 'The American proposal is still under review. Once we finalise our position, we will share it with Pakistan,' Iranian Foreign Ministry spokesman Esmaeil Baghaei said

key_facts.fact: Trump threatened to resume bombing at 'a much higher level and intensity' if Iran doesn't agree to the deal, posting on Truth Social: 'If they don't agree, the bombing starts.'
key_facts.excerpt: 'If they don't agree, the bombing starts,' Trump wrote... he said that depends on Iran accepting a reported agreement that he did not detail.

key_facts.fact: The US military fired on an Iranian oil tanker in the Gulf of Oman on May 7 — shooting out its rudder — as it attempted to breach the American naval blockade of Iran's ports.
key_facts.excerpt: the U.S. military fired on an Iranian oil tanker attempting to breach an American blockade of Iran's ports hours earlier... a U.S. fighter jet shot out the rudder of an Iranian oil tanker in the Gulf of Oman

key_facts.fact: Saudi Arabia and Kuwait lifted restrictions on US military use of their bases and airspace, and the Trump administration is now planning to restart Project Freedom to reopen the Strait of Hormuz.
key_facts.excerpt: The Wall Street Journal reported that Saudi Arabia and Kuwait have lifted those restrictions and that the Trump administration is now looking to restart Project Freedom in the coming days.

key_facts.fact: Senior Iranian official Mohsen Rezaee warned that Iran would not let the US reopen the strait with 'an unrealistic plan' and that any deal must include 'tangible benefits' for Iran.
key_facts.excerpt: Iranian lawmaker Ebrahim Rezaei... described the text as 'more of an American wish-list than a reality.'

key_facts.fact: Pakistan, mediating the talks, expressed optimism: 'We expect an agreement sooner rather than later,' said Foreign Ministry spokesperson Tahir Andrabi, while declining to disclose details.
key_facts.excerpt: 'We expect an agreement sooner rather than later,' Pakistan's Foreign Ministry spokesperson Tahir Andrabi said Thursday. 'We hope the parties will reach a peaceful and sustainable solution'
